newsitem.title: USA: Rep. Schaefer to try to stop U.S. reserve oil sale.
newsitem.headline: Rep. Schaefer to try to stop U.S. reserve oil sale.

text.p: The chairman of the U.S. House Commerce Energy subcommittee will try to block the sale of some $200 million of oil from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve called for in bills passed by the House and a Senate subcommittee, his spokeswoman said Friday.
"This is offensive and we will continue to work to have this taken out," a spokeswoman for Dan Schaefer, Colorado Republican, said.
The Senate Interior Appropriations Committee earlier Friday passed a bill that would sell $207.5 million worth of SPR oil next fiscal year to fund the reserves operations.
The House earlier this week passed its version of the bill that would sell $209 million of SPR oil.

Schaefer had tried unsuccessfully to remove the sale from the House bill then said he had an agreement with key lawmakers to work to get the sale removed from the bill when it was meshed with the Senate version in conference.
However having provisions for the sale in both bills would make that more difficult.
"It will be tough, but our policy hasn't changed at all. We're looking at our options to find out how we could have this language struck in the conference report," Schaefer's spokeswoman said.
The Senate panel's bill still has to move through the full Appropriations Committee, and then to the Senate floor, where changes could be made.

Sen. Slade Gorton, the Washington Republican who chairs the Interior appropriations subcommittee, said he hoped this would be the last such sale, but the panel could not find another way to meet members' spending priorities.
Senate Energy Committee Chairman Frank Murkowski, Republican of Alaska and the committee's ranking Democrat, Dale Bumpers of Arkansas, also oppose the sale.
